summary: Post-depot TPM microcode + BIOS firmware mismatch blocks Device Health Attestation and Intune compliance sensor registration
description:
Issue summary:
After a standard depot repair (SSD replacement + BIOS reflash) several devices fail to register the corporate Device Health Attestation (DHA) sensor with Intune. Device shows as non-compliant in console and Conditional Access blocks corporate app sign-in.

Impact:
- ~12 devices reported so far from us-west depot batch (engineering and sales laptops).
- Users are blocked from accessing corporate email and internal services due to Conditional Access requiring DHA compliance.
- Escalation requested by IT Ops because devices are stuck in staging and cannot be re-provisioned remotely.

Environment:
- Windows 11 Enterprise 22H2 builds patched to 2026-02 cumulative
- Devices were processed at central depot and had BIOS reflash to vendor-supplied image; TPM microcode patches applied via vendor firmware bundle.
- Intune + Endpoint Manager (prod, us-west)

Steps to reproduce (observed at least 3 times):
1) Device returned from depot with fresh OS image and BIOS image installed.
2) On first connect to corporate network and Intune enrollment, Device Health Attestation service fails to register the TPM attestation.
3) MDM shows sensor install OK but DHA status reports "AttestationFailed: TPM state inconsistency".
4) Conditional Access treats device as non-compliant; user cannot access O365 or internal web apps.

Observed behavior:
- Event Viewer: "DHA: Attestation response indicates invalid PCRs" (ID 42).
- System logs indicate TPM reported microcode level not matching expected inventory baseline.
- Intune logs show sensor installed but attestation handshake aborted (HTTP 401 from attestation service).

Expected behavior:
- Post-provisioning, devices should register DHA and report compliant state allowing Conditional Access to permit sign-in.

Notes:
- This differs from standard enrollment failures (network, broken SSO) because agent is present and network connectivity to attestation endpoints is validated.
- Suspected cause: vendor-supplied BIOS reflash applied a microcode revision that our DHA policy validator flags as unknown/unsupported, causing attestation to fail.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Ava Martinez: Ticket created after IT Ops batch report (10 devices). Initial triage assigned to firmware and intune owners.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Samuel O'Connor: Reproduced on a lab unit. Confirmed DHA register step fails with PCR mismatch. Captured Attestation XML and TPM event log. Attaching pointers to logs in investigation notes.

2026-03-10 12:30 - Priya Shah (SRE): Looked at attestation gateway logs; saw a pattern of rejected nonstandard microcode identifiers. Opening vendor support request with BIOS vendor and adding as blocker for depot imaging. (SRC: slack #internal-ops thread GHT3F4)

2026-03-11 08:46 - Samuel O'Connor: Temporary workaround identified: rolling back to previous BIOS microcode (vendor rollback image) on two lab units restored DHA registration — marking as workaround, not final fix.

2026-03-12 15:02 - Daniel Weber (Security): Recommend hold on further depot flashes for same SKU until vendor provides a signed microcode manifest that matches our attestation whitelist. Security will update compliance whitelist after vendor confirmation.
investigation_notes: Captured TPM event logs from affected units: PCR[0-7] values differ from baseline resulting in 'PCR mismatch' on attestation server. See /logs/tpm/pcr_dump_3094873.zip (internal storage).

Examined BIOS release notes from vendor - recent microcode patch includes CPU microcode CU_2026_03_01 which does not map to our DHA's allowed microcode registry values. Vendor used new microcode naming schema.

Ran 'Get-DeviceHealthAttestation' on impacted devices: AttestationServerResponse = 401 Unauthorized (token present) + 'InvalidPCRs' flag. Traced handshake to attestation gateway and confirmed gateway policy rejects the new microcode identifiers.
Tested rollback process: Reflashed BIOS to previous image from depot artifact store (rev 1.12) -> TPM reported expected microcode identifier -> DHA registration succeeded and device marked compliant.
Related artifact: internal PR updating attestation whitelist pending vendor signed manifest: GH-ops/attestation-whitelist-update#225 (link: https://github.com/redwood/ops/pull/225).
resolution: Workaround: Stop using vendor BIOS image CU_2026_03_01 for depot SKU. Use verified image rev 1.12 until vendor publishes a signed microcode manifest matching our whitelist.

Permanent fix path: Vendor to provide signed microcode manifest or we update attestation whitelist after security review. Security and Firmware teams to coordinate change window and communicate to depot ops.
Rollout notes: We have placed a temporary block on the depot imaging pipeline for affected SKUs. Depot Ops notified (ticket and slack).

Follow-up actions: (1) Vendor support case opened (VND-88821) requesting signed manifest and mapping of new microcode identifiers. (2) Add automated detection to depot job to validate microcode identifier against our whitelist before shipping. (3) Update runbook: confluence/runbooks/tpm-bios-firmware-mismatch with rollback steps and contact list.
